body:
With `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS=1`, `set_parent()` called the full `set_parents()` for `ordered_json` on every call: `push_back`/`emplace_back`, `at()`, and `operator[]`/`at()` on existing keys. Building an `ordered_json` array was therefore quadratic.

## Changes
- `at()` and array append set only the one child's `m_parent`.
- Object `operator[]`/`push_back`/`emplace` record the container capacity before the insert and call `set_parents()` only if it changed. Arrays and objects share one `container_capacity()` and one `set_parent_after_insert()` helper (arrays report their `capacity()`; for objects, only the node-based standard containers (`std::map`, `std::multimap`, `std::unordered_map`, `std::unordered_multimap`) report 0 = never moves, only `nlohmann::ordered_map` reports its `capacity()`, and any other object type reports unknown = always re-parent).
- `update()` (all overloads, incl. `merge_objects` and the iterative variant) now assigns through `operator[]` instead of calling `set_parent()` per key; `merge_patch()` already goes through `operator[]`, so it benefits too. `erase` keeps its `set_parents_after_object_erase()` (O(n) for `ordered_map` anyway).
- Remove the redundant `set_parents()` in the copy constructor (`copy_level`/`copy_iteratively` already re-parent each level). The move constructor keeps its `set_parents()` (required).
- New tests: parent-pointer invariant checker (`json` and `ordered_json`) across parse, copy, move, copy-assign, swap, push_back/emplace_back/emplace/operator[] growth and `at()`; `update()` (both overloads, `merge_objects`) and `merge_patch()` on `json`/`ordered_json` checking parents and diagnostic paths. No timing test (would be flaky).

## Numbers (ordered_json, nested-array push_back, -O2, diagnostics on)
| n | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 25k | 101 ms | ~8 ms |
| 50k | 412 ms | ~5 ms |
| 100k | 1635 ms | ~11 ms |
| 200k | 6482 ms | 27 ms |

`ordered_json::update()` with 20k new keys: 372 → 295 ms (no diagnostics: 259 ms), i.e. the diagnostics overhead is gone; the rest is `ordered_map`'s inherent linear key lookup (100k keys: 14.0 → 10.0 s).

`at(i)` x10000: 31.7 → 0.017 ms. Parse unchanged; copies −5–8 % with diagnostics.

## Breaking changes
None. No public API change; behaviour without `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS` is unchanged.

Tested with `-DJSON_DIAGNOSTICS=1`: unit-diagnostics, unit-ordered_json, unit-element_access1/2, unit-modifiers. `make amalgamate` run.

comments.body:
Reworked in c1d349338 (written by Claude Code, on Niels's behalf):

- **Missed site fixed:** `update_members` and `update_members_iteratively` called `set_parent()` per key, which re-parented the whole `ordered_json` each time. They now assign through `operator[]`, which re-parents everything only when the vector reallocated. `merge_patch()` already used `operator[]`, so it is covered. I found no other per-element `set_parent(` loops over objects or arrays.
- **Deduplicated:** `array_capacity`/`object_capacity` are now one `container_capacity()`, and the two after-insert helpers are one `set_parent_after_insert()`. `set_parent_plain` and `set_parent_at` are merged.
- **Tests:** `update()` (both overloads, with `merge_objects`) and `merge_patch()` on `json` and `ordered_json`, checking parent pointers and diagnostic paths.
- **Timing:** `ordered_json::update()` of 20k keys with diagnostics goes from 372 to 295 ms; without diagnostics it takes 259 ms. 100k keys goes from 14.0 to 10.0 s. What remains is the linear key lookup of `ordered_map`, not the parent updates.

unit-diagnostics passes. unit-modifiers and unit-ordered_json pass with and without `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS`.

review_comments.body: Should `detail::unknown_size()` be the default unless the container is known to not move?  In other words, we check for containers that we know don't move and return "may move" for everything else, rather than checking for containers that we know move, and return "won't move" for everything else?
Should these all say "the container" rather than "ordered_json"?

Agreed, and it was worse than it looked: `is_ordered_map` is just `has_capacity`, so in that overload the check was always false, and every object type without `capacity()` counted as "never moves". Fixed in 80692a15a. Only `std::map`, `std::multimap`, `std::unordered_map` and `std::unordered_multimap` count as stable (new `detail::has_stable_elements`), and only the real `nlohmann::ordered_map` has its capacity tracked (new `detail::is_nlohmann_ordered_map`). Everything else is treated as "may move". That also covers a sorted flat map that has `capacity()` but shifts members on a middle insert. The new test uses an object type that moves its members without changing its capacity; it fails without the change.

*(Written by Claude Code on my behalf.)*

Done. `set_parents_after_object_erase()` now re-parents unless `has_stable_elements<object_t>`. After this PR, `set_parent()` had no callers left, so I removed it instead of changing it (80692a15a).

*(Written by Claude Code on my behalf.)*

Yes, reworded to "the object type" in both `update()` comments (80692a15a).

*(Written by Claude Code on my behalf.)*

title: Fix quadratic parent updates for ordered_json with JSON_DIAGNOSTICS
